# Azure Functions Validation

> Validation and serialization layer for the Azure Functions Python v2 programming model.

Part of the **Azure Functions Python DX Toolkit**. Pydantic-powered request validation and response serialization for HTTP-triggered functions — validate body, query, path, and header parameters with a decorator, bringing a FastAPI-like developer experience to Azure Functions. Install from PyPI with `pip install azure-functions-validation`.

## Getting Started
- [Installation](https://yeongseon.dev/azure-functions-python/validation/installation/): Install the package.
- [Quickstart](https://yeongseon.dev/azure-functions-python/validation/getting-started/): Minimal end-to-end example.
- [Configuration](https://yeongseon.dev/azure-functions-python/validation/configuration/): Customize validation behavior.
- [Strict API Boundary Models](https://yeongseon.dev/azure-functions-python/validation/strict-models/): Choose strict JSON body models without breaking string-based query, path, and header inputs.
- Custom formatters receive original 4xx exceptions and sanitized 5xx errors by default.
- Opt-in body policies return 413 for `max_body_bytes` and 415 for non-JSON
  non-empty bodies under `require_json_content_type`; defaults preserve current behavior.
- Validated responses support `response_by_alias`, `response_exclude_none`, and
  `response_exclude_unset`; these require `response_model` and do not apply to
  direct `HttpResponse` returns.
- Custom adapters raise `MalformedRequestError` for malformed syntax (400) and
  `AdapterValidationError` for validation failures (422); other exceptions are
  logged and sanitized as 500.
- Adapter instances are shared across concurrent invocations and must be
  stateless or thread-safe. Validate implementations with
  `AdapterConformanceTests` from the public testing surface.
